author: Mexico Daily Post
title: Kuri Shields Querétaro-U.S. Security Ties Amid Federal Scrutiny of Police Academy
text:
QUERÉTARO, MEXICO — Governor Mauricio Kuri González has moved to de-escalate growing tensions with the federal government over the establishment of the International Academy of Police Training, asserting that his administration remains committed to a close and collaborative relationship with the presidency.
The governor’s remarks come in response to recent criticisms from President Claudia Sheinbaum, who emphasized that any international cooperation regarding security must strictly adhere to federal procedures. Kuri responded by clarifying that the state of Querétaro understands these requirements and intends to operate within the established federal framework moving forward.
“I believe Querétaro has a very good relationship with the federation,” Kuri stated during the presentation of the XVIII National Award for Social Oversight. He highlighted the state’s long-standing cooperation with various international partners, specifically noting the strong ties maintained with the United States Embassy.
The governor also sought to downplay recent controversy surrounding the “laying of the first stone” for the new academy. He clarified that the event was purely symbolic and did not involve the signing of any formal agreements or the participation of foreign agents. Kuri maintained that the State Secretariat of Foreign Affairs had been informed of the ceremony in advance.
“It was a protocolary act; nothing was signed,” Kuri explained, adding that the state will follow all federal mandates once the specific curriculum and training plans are finalized.
To further reassure the federal government, Kuri revealed that he has been in direct communication with both the Secretary of Foreign Affairs and the Secretary of Security. According to the governor, these officials have offered support to ensure the project aligns with national security interests, particularly in any instances of training that may require oversight by the federal high-security cabinet.
While navigating the federal government’s demands for oversight, Kuri defended the necessity of international cooperation. He argued that these partnerships have been instrumental in training local police and remains a vital component of the state’s strategy to bolster public safety.
“Everything that is done in favor of security is never enough,” Kuri said, signaling his intent to continue seeking external resources while maintaining a cooperative stance with Mexico City.
